newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda army says at least 50 rebels killed.
newsitem.headline: Uganda army says at least 50 rebels killed.

text.p: Uganda's army said fighting raged with Ugandan rebel forces on Thursday after at least 50 rebels were killed in the southwestern Kasese region bordering on Zaire.

An army spokesman, speaking by telephone from Kasese, said Ugandan troops were battling rebels of the mainly Moslem Allied Democratic Force (ADF), which Uganda says is backed by renegade Zairean soldiers.

He said at least 50 "invaders" were killed on Wednesday and five Ugandan soldiers and three civilians were wounded in the fighting on Ugandan territory, which followed a Ugandan army thrust into northeast Zaire from the Kasese region last week.
But civilians fleeing the area gave a civilian death toll of between three and five and said many others were wounded.

The spokesman said Ugandan troops heavily shelled Zaire on Tuesday and Wednesday and were likely to do so again on Thursday if rebel attacks on Ugandan positions persisted. He named the shelled Zairean villages as Lume, Lungese, Mulamba and Bukyira.
"We shelled these areas and are now waiting to hear the results," he added.
Officers said 100 Ugandan rebels based in Zaire attacked army positions on Tuesday night and fighting was around three Ugandan villages near Kasese, the southwest provincial capital.
Kasese residents said hundreds of people had fled the area and heavy artillery fire was audible from the distance.

Fighting has raged in the southwest since last week when Ugandan troops crossed into Zaire with the blessing of President Yoweri Museveni, saying they were pursuing rebels. The Ugandan army says its troops only went three-km (two-miles) into Zaire.
Kasese residents said rebel gangs had set their homes on fire as a punishment for supporting the government troops.
Zaire accuses Uganda, Burundi and Rwanda of sending troops to fight alongside rebels who have seized a front 550-km (340- miles) long running north-south parallel to Zaire's eastern border.

Army officers said the Ugandan rebels were trapped and killed in the southwestern hilly country of Buswange, Kisekere and Kyabitondo. Remaining rebel forces had fled back into eastern Zaire, they added.

Amia Gasende, who fled the fighting, said: "Our homes have been set on fire by the rebels. They have accused local people of joining hands with the UPDF (government Uganda Peoples' Defence Force) to track them down."
"The rebels have told our neighbours that they will return under cover of darkness and kill us all," Gasende added.
President Museveni, who is in the northern Ugandan town of Gulu, has made no comment on the fighting in the southwest.

But the former rebel leader faces embarrassment in Kampala, where his senior defence adviser resigned on Wednesday after sharply criticising the president for mismanaging a separate war against rebels in the north.

The adviser, Major-General David Tunyefunza, told a parliamentary committee that if Museveni's government had failed to win its 10-year low-scale civil war in the north and refused to talk peace with the rebels "it should pack up and quit".
Museveni says rebels in the north are backed by neighbouring Sudan and has repeatedly vowed to defeat them militarily.
Uganda's military high command has called a meeting on Friday to discuss Tunyefunza's resignation and the fighting.
